original_value: The importance of body area sensor networks (BASNs) is increasing day by day because of their increasing use in Internet of things (IoT)-enabled healthcare application services. They help humans in improving their quality of life by continuously monitoring various vital signs through biosensors strategically placed on the human body. However, BASNs face serious challenges, in terms of the short life span of their batteries and unreliable data transmission, because of the highly unstable and unpredictable channel conditions of tiny biosensors located on the human body. These factors may result in poor data gathering quality in BASNs. Therefore, a more reliable data transmission mechanism is greatly needed in order to gather quality data in BASN-based healthcare applications. Therefore, this study proposes a novel, multiobjective, lion mating optimization inspired routing protocol, called self-organizing multiobjective routing protocol (SARP), for BASN-based IoT healthcare applications. The proposed routing scheme significantly reduces local search problems and finds the best dynamic cluster-based routing solutions between the source and destination in BASNs. Thus, it significantly improves the overall packet delivery rate, residual energy, and throughput with reduced latency and packet error rates in BASNs. Extensive simulation results validate the performance of our proposed SARP scheme against the existing routing protocols in terms of the packet delivery ratio, latency, packet error rate, throughput, and energy efficiency for BASN-based health monitoring applications.

result.paraphrase: The growing use of Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled healthcare services is making body area sensor networks (BASNs) increasingly important. By continuously tracking vital signs with biosensors strategically placed on the human body, they help improve human quality of life. However, BASNs also face major challenges because the tiny body-worn biosensors operate under highly unstable and unpredictable channel conditions, which lead to short battery life and unreliable data transmission. As a result, data collection quality in BASNs can be poor. To address this need for more dependable transmission, this study presents a new multiobjective routing protocol inspired by lion mating optimization, called the self-organizing multiobjective routing protocol (SARP), for BASN-based IoT healthcare applications. The proposed scheme greatly reduces local search issues and identifies the best dynamic cluster-based routing solutions between source and destination in BASNs. In turn, it substantially improves packet delivery rate, residual energy, and throughput while reducing latency and packet error rates. Extensive simulation results confirm that the proposed SARP scheme outperforms existing routing protocols in packet delivery ratio, latency, packet error rate, throughput, and energy efficiency for BASN-based health monitoring applications.
